summary: Need clearer error messages + retry guidance: mixed 500/502/503 under burst traffic (Hosted API)
description:
Customer (HarborView Analytics, enterprise Hosted API) is observing intermittent request failures during predictable burst traffic (batch jobs / scheduled report generation). They are seeing a mix of HTTP 500/502/503 responses and timeouts and asked for:

1) Clearer error messages so they can distinguish "our bug" vs "platform overload / temporary capacity".
2) Explicit retry guidance (when to retry, how long to wait, whether to retry streaming requests).
3) Confirmation whether these failed requests count toward billing.

Impact:
- Their job runner treats any 5xx as retryable and immediately retries without jitter.
- Under spikes this appears to amplify failures (retry storm), leading to a longer recovery window.
- They are also using our OpenAI-compatible endpoint in one service and Redwood SDK in another; they want consistent error shapes.

Environment:
- Hosted API, prod, region: us-east
- Models: rw-chat-3.5 (chat/completions), rw-embed-2 (embeddings)
- Traffic pattern: step-function increase (approx. 10x baseline) around 00:00–00:10 UTC, sustained for ~8–12 minutes

Examples provided by customer:
- 503 Service Unavailable with body sometimes empty, sometimes gateway HTML (likely upstream 502/503)
- 502 Bad Gateway for a subset of streaming requests (disconnect mid-stream)
- 500 Internal Server Error with request_id present but no actionable error code

Sample request IDs (from customer):
- req_01JCTK9R8S9K1W2W5D9GQ3GZP7
- req_01JCTK9S2W4Q7ZBJP8N2G4H1VN
- req_01JCTK9T0K7J2D4W1F0VQ8E3YQ

Asks:
- Provide recommended retry/backoff strategy (incl. jitter) and guidance on max retries / deadlines.
- Confirm whether customer should treat these as transient (retry) vs hard-fail.
- Provide timeline on improvements to overload behavior / standardized error codes.

Notes:
- This appears related to the ongoing reliability work on hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (better 429/503 semantics, Retry-After, consistent error taxonomy).
comments:
2025-11-18 10:22 PT — Dev Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Asked customer for (a) approximate timestamps with timezone, (b) region + model, (c) whether requests were streaming, (d) a few request_ids, and (e) whether they are retrying on 5xx and at what cadence.

Also shared interim best practice: exponential backoff with jitter, cap retries, avoid concurrent fan-out retries, and honor any Retry-After header if present (not consistently emitted yet).

2025-11-18 12:05 PT — Customer (HarborView): Shared timestamps (00:02–00:09 UTC), confirmed prod us-east. They are retrying immediately up to 8 times with constant 250ms delay and no jitter. Streaming requests are retried the same way. They confirmed mix of OpenAI-compat endpoint and Redwood SDK (Python).

2025-11-18 13:10 PT — Owen Phillips (Support Eng): Pulled logs for provided request_ids. Pattern looks like overload-induced upstream failures and gateway timeouts; error mapping is inconsistent (some upstream 503, some 502 from gateway when upstream closed, some 500 when internal timeout path). Looping in SRE for confirmation and guidance.

Links:
- #support thread: slack/support/thread-1720796622
- #incidents context: slack/incidents/thread-1720861145

2025-11-19 09:02 PT — Christine Wong (SRE): Confirmed us-east experienced brief saturation around the window; routing/control-plane remained healthy but runtime queues grew and several services fell back to generic 5xx. This is exactly what the "Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding" effort is meant to fix (layered shedding + stable error semantics).

Interim guidance:
- Treat current 5xx/timeouts during this window as transient.
- Reduce retry aggressiveness immediately (they are amplifying load).
- For streaming: do not blindly retry mid-stream without idempotency; prefer restarting the request with a new request_id and a capped retry budget.

SRE note: once the standardized overload responses roll out, they should expect 429 (overload admission) or 503 (temporarily unavailable) with Redwood-specific error codes + Retry-After.

2025-11-19 09:40 PT — Dev Patel (Support): Sent customer a concrete retry recommendation:
- Use exponential backoff with jitter (full jitter or equal jitter).
- Start at 500ms–1s, max backoff 15–30s.
- Max retries: 5 (or total retry time budget 60–90s) for chat; embeddings can tolerate longer budgets.
- Respect Retry-After header when present.
- Add circuit-breaking on client side: if >X% requests fail for Y seconds, slow down and alert.
- Ensure concurrency caps so retries do not increase overall in-flight requests.

Also clarified: failed requests that return an error are not billed as successful token usage; however, they may still see network egress / client-side costs. (Billing team note: we only bill for successfully completed inference; partial streaming failures are not charged for un-delivered tokens.)

2025-11-20 11:15 PT — Customer (HarborView): Asked for exact error shapes/status codes they should key off of, and whether OpenAI-compat endpoint will return the same Retry-After header + structured error body.

2025-11-20 12:30 PT — Brian Murphy (API Semantics): Answered with planned behavior (pending rollout):
- Overload admission shed at edge: HTTP 429 with Redwood error code (e.g., OVERLOADED_ADMISSION) and Retry-After.
- Capacity / breaker open: HTTP 503 with Redwood error code (e.g., OVERLOADED_CAPACITY / BREAKER_OPEN) and Retry-After.
- Gateway will stop returning ambiguous 502/HTML and instead return JSON error bodies for API endpoints.
- OpenAI-compat will map into OpenAI-style error objects while preserving Retry-After.

Referenced ADR-0147 for the formal mapping and stated docs will be published before broad rollout.

2025-11-22 14:05 PT — Owen Phillips (Support Eng): Provided customer with a preview of the recommended parsing contract:
- Always read HTTP status + Retry-After if present.
- Prefer Redwood error code in JSON body (or OpenAI-compat error.type) for programmatic handling.
- Retryable: overload/capacity/breaker-open codes.
- Non-retryable: auth errors, invalid_request, insufficient_quota, and safety/policy blocks.

Suggested they upgrade SDKs when released (Python/TS) to get first-class access to Retry-After and overload error codes.

2025-12-03 09:18 PT — Dev Patel (Support): Notified customer that the public docs PR is in review and SDK updates are landing to expose Retry-After and overload codes cleanly. Shared links (non-sensitive):
- Docs: github/redwood-docs/pr-912
- Python SDK: github/redwood-sdk-python/pr-522
- TS SDK: github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-418

Asked customer if they can test new backoff settings in their next scheduled burst and report whether failure duration improves.

2025-12-05 08:41 PT — Customer (HarborView): Confirmed that after implementing exponential backoff with jitter and lowering concurrency, the burst window still has some 503s but recovery is faster and their job completes without manual intervention. They requested to be notified when standardized error codes + Retry-After are fully rolled out in us-east.

2025-12-06 10:10 PT — Owen Phillips (Support Eng): Marking resolved with action items tracked under reliability initiative. Customer has mitigation in place; follow-up will happen via release notes/docs once rollout completes in us-east. Added note to CS to proactively notify customer when overload protection is enabled for their primary routes.
resolution:
Provided interim guidance to mitigate retry storms (exponential backoff with jitter, capped retries/time budget, concurrency limits; streaming-specific cautions). SRE confirmed failures aligned with a brief us-east overload window and that ongoing Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding work will standardize customer-facing overload responses.

Planned/communicated behavior (per ADR-0147): consistent JSON error payloads, Redwood overload error codes, and Retry-After header across Hosted + OpenAI-compatible endpoints (mapping into OpenAI-style error objects). Customer confirmed improved stability after client-side retry/concurrency changes. Follow-up notifications to occur when standardized overload errors are fully rolled out in us-east.
internal_notes:
Key takeaway: customer’s immediate constant-delay retries worsened the spike. This ticket is useful for validating docs/SDK messaging. Consider adding a docs callout: "Do not retry immediately on 5xx; add jitter." Also ensure gateway never returns HTML for API routes.

If customer reports renewed issues post-rollout: check for client retry loop (see SUP-3974 pattern) and verify Retry-After is being honored.
next_steps:
1) Support/CS to notify HarborView when overload protection is enabled in us-east for rw-chat-3.5 and OpenAI-compat endpoints.
2) Ensure docs explicitly cover streaming retry guidance and idempotency caveats.
3) Track any additional request_ids from the next spike to validate error-code coverage (no generic 500/502) once rollout is enabled.
